extracted.intended_audience: creative writing program directors, faculty, and graduate/undergraduate students
extracted.subtask_description: Program-level hallmarks describing pedagogy, curricular expectations, faculty qualifications, and student outcomes for serious creative-writing programs (MFA/BFA/BA/low-residency). Emphasizes workshop pedagogy, curricular breadth, faculty mentorship, and qualities of 'publishable' work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Workshop-Based Instruction
rubrics_metrics.description: Workshop-based instruction characterized by peer critique, iterative revision, practical craft over theoretical analysis, and manuscript-focused discussion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programs should center learning in workshops where students give and receive peer feedback, revise repeatedly, focus on craft techniques rather than abstract theory, and discuss students' manuscripts in concrete, actionable ways.

rubrics_metrics.name: Curricular Diversity Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Curriculum must include multiple literary periods, multicultural American (and global) traditions, varied craft topics, and genre breadth (fiction, poetry, CNF, drama, screenwriting).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Course offerings and requirements should ensure historical range, cross-cultural perspectives, a range of craft skills, and exposure to multiple genres so students develop breadth as well as depth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Faculty Standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Faculty should excel at both holistic and line-specific revision suggestions, be active publishing/practicing writers, and function as mentors rather than relying solely on lecture-based teaching.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hiring and evaluation should prioritize instructors who can give substantive, craft-oriented feedback at both macro and micro levels, maintain an active professional writing practice, and engage students in sustained mentorship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student Graduation Standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Students (for graduation) must produce a publishable literary work, demonstrate expertise in a primary genre, and engage with secondary genres.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program outcomes and culminating projects (e.g., thesis/manuscript) should show readiness for publication, clear mastery of the declared genre, and evidence of cross-genre competency or exploration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinctive Voice
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publishable work is expected to show an individual, recognizable voice that sets the work apart from generic or imitative writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sentence-level Mastery
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High-quality writing demonstrates precise, controlled sentence craft — clarity, rhythm, diction, and syntactic choices that serve the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Earned Formal Control
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form and structure should feel intentional and justified by content; formal experiments must be supported by the work’s aims rather than arbitrary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ambition of Subject
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work should address substantive, consequential, or challenging subjects — showing intellectual and emotional reach rather than triviality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Craft Choices that Fit the Work
rubrics_metrics.description: Craft choices that fit the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Techniques, voice, form, and other craft decisions should be appropriate to the material and contribute coherently to the piece’s effects and meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality Balanced with Tradition-awareness
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strong work innovates while acknowledging or engaging the literary traditions it draws from—newness informed by knowledge of antecedents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revision-evidenced (multiple drafts visible)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence of iterative revision — multiple drafts, substantive changes, and responsive development — is expected as a marker of craft seriousness and maturation of the work.
